artists.biography: Lesoir Lesoir began as a project of 5 befriended musicians who had gained valuable previous experience in other bands. It was when this group toured together through England in June 2009, that their desire came to combine their creativity and form a new band. From that point on, the 5 members have played intensively in different cities in order to stay creative and productive. During these sessions in Maastricht, Amsterdam and Leuven, the songs have slowly evolved from tiny bits of music into a coherent full length album that has now been recorded together with producer Rudy Coclet (Arno) in the Jet Studio in Bruxelles, Belgium. The new album successfully combines all of the creative tensions between each individual in the band and the producer. The songs of Lesoir are heavy but with a lot of room for dynamics and atmosphere. A raw, pure, dark sound with emotion as its centre. Lesoir's set goes from fragility and whispering, to chaos and heavy sounds, without losing the melody of each song. With hints of Skunk Anansie, A Perfect Circle and Soundgarden. From 2010 on Lesoir will present itself with their debut album and a very special unique live show in which visuals and sound will enhance each other. Despite the short period of time in which the band has formed and recorded their music, Lesoir is ready for its audience. Why wait..? Lesoir is Vocals: Maartje Meessen Guitar: Ingo Dassen Guitar: Nick Franssen Bass: Alex van Damme Drums: Ruben van Asselt Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Lesoir - IV Latitude (2017)

Released in November 2017 on Gentle Art of Music, IV Latitude represents a significant artistic evolution for Dutch progressive rock band Lesoir. The album marks a deliberate shift in the band's sonic direction, with producers John Cornfield (known for work with Muse, Oasis, and Stone Roses) and Pineapple Thief frontman Bruce Soord guiding the sessions toward a more melodically-focused approach. Rather than abandoning their metal roots entirely, Lesoir tempered the angular aggression of previous releases in favor of progressive arrangements that prioritize compositional sophistication and emotional resonance.

The album showcases the band's expanded instrumental palette, featuring dual female vocalists in Maartje Meessen and Eleen Bartholomeus alongside guitars, keyboards, flute, and piano. Musically, IV Latitude blends theatrical progressive elements with dreamy soundscapes and orchestral string arrangements, drawing comparisons to the band Magenta while maintaining its own identity. The production quality and band maturity evident throughout the record demonstrate considerable growth compared to their 2015 predecessor Luctor Et Emergo.

Critical reception positioned IV Latitude as a substantial step forward for the band, with reviewers noting its accessibility to a broader audience without sacrificing progressive complexity. The album's intricate arrangements and layered compositions reward repeated listening, establishing a more defined sonic character that solidified Lesoir's standing within the progressive rock landscape.
